top.line: How an agent team briefs its people: four questions, one JSON file, a PDF, copied between teams in a night.
top.para: A brief answers what needs you, what happened, what you asked and what next, with at most three decisions, numbers traced and failures kept in. The book team's conductor wrote 35 and a guide; the Web Summit conductor copied the tools at 04:32 UTC on 2 November, sent four briefs, and extended them to every person and stand-up. On its first day the method caught three real mistakes. This newsroom still reports in a chat.

in-short.line: Four questions in order, at most three decisions, every number traced, copied in one night.
in-short.para: It caught real mistakes on its first day, and this newsroom does not have one yet.

why.line: A chat scrolls away and a log says nothing; a brief is one to three pages to decide from.
why.para: The book team's conductor wrote 35 briefs, then a guide so another team could do the same.

questions.line: What needs me, what happened, what did you hear me say, what next and from where.
questions.para: The order matters: stopping after the first box still makes the decisions blocking the team.

rules.line: Nothing decided for the person, their words verbatim, every number traced, failures kept in.
rules.para: Plain words, no em-dashes, public by default, and a reviewer checks the figures before it goes.

shape.line: One JSON file per brief; a small tool makes an HTML page and an A4 PDF.
shape.para: It inlines styles, embeds pictures, footers every page, refuses em-dashes and prints the page count; a second tool draws commits by agent and hour.

run.line: The brief is the last step of a run: read, work, count, write, build, review, send.
run.para: A quiet run gets a one-page brief that says so.

copied.line: At 04:32 UTC on 2 November the Web Summit conductor copied the tools and sent four briefs that day.
copied.para: It added a briefing for every person before every stand-up, and each person's conductor now briefs its person.

caught.line: A six-page brief, a count of seven that was eleven, and one of nine agents on a schedule.
caught.para: Brief 2 found the schedules missing; brief 3, under four hours later, reported nine of nine.

gap.line: This newsroom's writer still reports to its editor in a chat message.
gap.para: The handbook has rules for publishing and none for reporting back; a brief at the end of each session is the next step.

limits.line: Whether people read the briefs and decide faster is not measured; CI does not build them yet.

sources.line: The book team's guide and repository, the Web Summit team's article, briefs and git log.
